key_themes: Semiconductor sell-off on AI capex overhang — TSMC raised CapEx to $60-64B despite Q2 beat, dragging chip sector down 3%+
Alphabet loses $200B market cap as Bloomberg reports Gemini 3.5 Pro is months behind schedule with key DeepMind talent departing
Strong diversified earnings from UnitedHealth, United Airlines, J.B. Hunt, and BlackRock provide pockets of strength amid tech weakness
Oil tops $80/barrel for 4th consecutive session as US airstrikes on Iranian military sites escalate Strait of Hormuz supply fears
Wave of analyst actions: Capital One upgrades PANW and OKTA in cybersecurity; Truist slaps Sell on Lululemon

stocks.discussion_driver: TSMC fell ~4% despite a record Q2 earnings beat, as its raised CapEx guidance to $60-64B (up from $52-56B) spooked investors about AI spending sustainability, dragging the broader semiconductor index down over 3%. The stock is being pulled between its dominant AI-era position and near-term capital allocation concerns.
bull_case: AI-driven chip demand is accelerating, with TSMC posting its largest YoY revenue increase in 2026 and a 77% profit jump in Q2, confirming its indispensable role in the global AI supply chain
Unrivaled foundry leadership at advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm) with no credible competition ensures dominant market share and premium pricing power for the foreseeable future
bear_case: Raised CapEx guidance to $60-64B pressures near-term return on invested capital and free cash flow conversion, fueling investor concern about AI capex sustainability
Elevated geopolitical risk from Taiwan-China tensions remains an existential tail risk for the world's most critical semiconductor supply chain

stocks.discussion_driver: UnitedHealth surged 7%+ in early trading after a massive Q2 beat (adj. EPS $6.38 vs. $4.90 estimated, revenue $112.03B vs. $110.85B expected), sending shares to a 15-month high intraday at $461. The company raised full-year EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00, with multiple major Wall Street firms lifting price targets to the $430-$492 range.
bull_case: Massive Q2 beat (adj. EPS $6.38 vs. $4.90 estimate) with raised FY 2026 guidance to $19.50-$20.00 signals strong earnings momentum and a compelling operational recovery
Diversified healthcare platform spanning insurance, pharmacy benefits, and care delivery provides durable, recurring cash flows that are resilient across market cycles
bear_case: Stock faces ongoing scrutiny over medical cost ratio trends and significant regulatory/political risk to Medicare Advantage reimbursement rates
Trailing P/E of ~32x represents an elevated valuation for a healthcare insurer operating in a complex and politically sensitive regulatory environment

stocks.discussion_driver: Alphabet dropped 4.4%, erasing ~$200B in market cap, after Bloomberg reported that its Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model is months behind schedule and key DeepMind researchers — including Transformer co-inventor Noam Shazeer — have departed for rivals, raising serious doubts about Alphabet's ability to maintain AI leadership at a critical competitive inflection point.
bull_case: Google Cloud and AI monetization generated 82% YoY quarterly earnings growth, demonstrating the core business remains highly profitable and growing despite competitive pressures
Google Search retains ~90% global market share with compounding advertising revenues, providing a deeply entrenched competitive moat that will take years to meaningfully erode
bear_case: Gemini 3.5 Pro reportedly months behind schedule with key DeepMind researchers (including Transformer co-inventor Noam Shazeer) departing to rivals, directly threatening Alphabet's AI leadership narrative at a critical inflection point
DOJ antitrust pressure on the Search monopoly creates structural risk, with potential forced changes to distribution agreements that underpin its dominant advertising revenue base

stocks.discussion_driver: J.B. Hunt surged in premarket trading after Q2 EPS of $1.91 beat estimates by 12% and revenue grew 19% YoY to $3.5B; management cited accelerating intermodal demand throughout the quarter. Multiple analysts raised price targets post-earnings, though Morgan Stanley was a notable outlier downgrading to Underweight with a $200 target.
bull_case: Q2 EPS of $1.91 beat estimates by 12% with revenue up 19% YoY to $3.5B, signaling a robust freight cycle recovery with accelerating intermodal volumes and strong operational leverage
Accelerating intermodal demand and record shareholder returns position JBHT as a prime beneficiary of continued supply chain normalization and infrastructure investment tailwinds
bear_case: Trailing P/E of ~42.5x is a premium valuation that leaves limited margin of safety if freight demand normalizes or macro conditions deteriorate in H2 2026
Morgan Stanley downgraded to Underweight with a $200 price target (~27% downside from current levels), citing valuation excess and risk of post-cycle earnings mean reversion

stocks.discussion_driver: GE Aerospace beat Q2 estimates (adj. EPS $2.02 vs. $1.86 est., revenue $12.63B vs. $11.86B est.) and raised FY 2026 EPS guidance to $7.65-$7.85, but shares initially fell ~4% as investors focused on an elevated CapEx outlook before recovering to close modestly higher on the day. 19 of 21 covering analysts maintain Buy or Strong Buy ratings.
bull_case: Record Q2 beat with raised FY 2026 EPS guidance to $7.65-$7.85 reflects strong commercial aerospace aftermarket demand and disciplined cost execution across LEAP and GE9X engine platforms
Booming commercial and defense aerospace demand with long-cycle engine aftermarket services provides high-visibility, recurring revenue streams well into the next decade
bear_case: Forward P/E of ~48x is well above the sector average of ~21x, pricing in substantial growth and leaving minimal room for execution shortfalls or demand disappointment
Elevated CapEx outlook triggered an initial ~4% post-earnings sell-off, signaling investor concern about free cash flow conversion pace relative to the aggressive guidance raise
